decisions.diagnosis: On its first day the counter reported exact zeros in both directions from 05:00 to 19:00 and then resumed normal counts, which looks like installation or commissioning downtime; the riders who passed are not recoverable.
decisions.evidence: Both directions had 1-2 bikes per slot before 05:00, then 0 until 19:15, then 5 or more per slot again; the next day totalled 1105 bikes; neighbour 551 recorded 1040 that day.

decisions.diagnosis: Both directions reported exact zeros for five and a half days, weekdays included, while neighbours counted normally; there was no trickle of riders as there is during this site's known closures, so the counter was down and the counts cannot be recovered.
decisions.evidence: The day before: 1997 bikes; Feb 12-15: 0/0/0/0; neighbours 545 at 331-751 and 551 at 589-1229 per day; counts resumed at 15:15 on Feb 16.

decisions.diagnosis: Both directions reported exact zeros through the whole weekday morning peak and came back around 10:30, while Castlereagh St (545) counted its usual morning; this looks like an outage, though a short morning closure cannot be ruled out.
decisions.evidence: 340 hours 5-9 were 0 (the usual 8am hour is about 50-120); 545 recorded 25 bikes in its 8am hour; no rain.

decisions.diagnosis: On isolated days the feed published every one of the 4 channel records twice, which doubles the day's total; neighbours 545 and 551 double on the same days, so this is a feed repeat.
decisions.evidence: duplicates(): 16 day-runs (e.g. 2024-01-09: 4737 bikes against about 2300 on the days around it; 1188 and 1178 repeated bikes); every extra record exactly repeats another; days include 2022-04-10, 06-06, 06-21, 07-31, 09-08, 09-10, 2023-02-14, 10-06, 12-08, 2024-01-09, 01-22, 02-26, 03-24/25, 06-23/24, 06-30/07-01, 08-01/02.

decisions.diagnosis: The counter cut out in the middle of the morning peak and reported exact zeros in both directions for 5.5 months, resuming on the same morning as Kent St (551), which had also been at zero; nothing was counted, so the period is unrecoverable.
decisions.evidence: At 07:30 on 2023-03-01 there were 15 bikes/slot, then 0 in every slot until 08:30 on 2023-08-18; the week before averaged about 2000 bikes/day; 545 counted about 700-1100/day throughout.

decisions.diagnosis: The sensor failed intermittently: most slots read zero, with occasional isolated bursts, for eight days in both directions, while the neighbouring sites were normal; the few counts left do not show how many riders passed.
decisions.evidence: Daily totals Dec 8-15: 750 (partly duplicated), 55, 1, 54, 142, 33, 19, 33, against about 2300 on weekdays before and after; 545 and 551 were normal (about 900-1600 per day); hours with counts show isolated bursts such as 58 then 0.

decisions.diagnosis: A block of exact zeros ran from midnight to the next day's early morning in both directions, which is an outage and not recoverable.
decisions.evidence: Every slot 0 on 12-27 (neighbours 545=572, 551=870); normal counts before and after (1551 and 1766 bikes).

decisions.diagnosis: A block of exact zeros ran from midnight to the next day's early morning in both directions, which is an outage and not recoverable.
decisions.evidence: Every slot 0 on 12-30 (neighbours 545=561, 551=856); 1944 bikes on 12-29 and 1198 on 12-31.

decisions.diagnosis: A block of exact zeros ran from midnight to the next day's early morning in both directions, which is an outage and not recoverable.
decisions.evidence: Every slot 0 on Friday 02-23 (neighbours 545=811, 551=1381); 2438 bikes the day before and 1597 on Saturday.

decisions.diagnosis: The sensor degraded: hours of zero were scattered through busy periods in both directions, getting worse until the counter read zero for six full days, and it came back at the normal level on 03-17; the counts that remain undercount by an unknown amount.
decisions.evidence: 340 had zero hours at 7-8 and 17-18 on 03-03, then daily totals of 459, 371, 250, 118 and 369 against about 1100; both directions were exact 0 from 03-11 to 03-16; neighbours were normal (545 about 1000-1170 per day).

decisions.diagnosis: Counter 228 came back after a gap in data only to publish exact zeros in both directions for 5.5 months until it was replaced; it was dead, and there are no counts to recover.
decisions.evidence: Every slot 0 from 2024-12-31 to 2025-06-12, against about 2000-2400/day before; 545 counted about 900-1100/day in Jan-Mar 2025.

decisions.diagnosis: A network-wide feed outage: every record from counter 357 that day is a 'warning' zero, and nothing is recoverable.
decisions.evidence: All 192 records have status warning with a count of 0; network() shows 37 sites at zero that day; the days either side had about 2900-3000 bikes.

series.name: Morning-peak direction (228 East), 2016-2024
series.evidence: The old Ecocounter's direction with the AM peak. It is kept apart from 357/1752, which carries the same AM-peak flow (labelled West): the 14-month gap and the change of counter, while the neighbouring counters were replaced too, mean comparability cannot be checked (Apr 2024: 2241/day, Apr 2026: 3520/day, both directions combined).

series.name: Evening-peak direction (228 West), 2016-2024
series.evidence: The old counter's PM-peak direction in every era. The 2021 swap in which direction is larger comes from the AM peak collapsing during COVID, not from a label change.

series.name: Morning-peak direction (357 West), 2025-
series.evidence: The new Metrocount's AM-peak direction (8am hour 207 against 92). It matches the flow of 228/340 despite the opposite label, but its level cannot be compared to 228 across the gap.

series.name: Evening-peak direction (357 East), 2025-
series.evidence: The new counter's PM-peak direction (5pm hour 243 against 132). It matches the flow of 228/341 despite the opposite label; kept separate because comparability across the counter change is unknown.

useful: overview: showed the dead-zero periods, the months with extra records and the direction-balance shift at a glance
zeros(counter=True): listed every outage and weekend closure with its exact bounds
duplicates: found the whole-day feed repeats precisely
compare(by='day'): separated closures and outages at this site from network events, and showed 545 and 551 doubling on the same days
hourly: showed that the direction labels of 228 and 357 are reversed relative to each other (AM-peak flow)
network: confirmed that 2025-10-23 was a feed-wide outage
not_useful: channels: the four records per slot carry no channel identifier, and their ID order is not stable, so a dead channel cannot be traced
spikes: mostly flagged late-night duplicate slots and small real bursts
improve: zeros: add a flag for whether the stretch had any non-zero trickle nearby (a closure) or exact zeros (an outage), and the neighbours' counts over the same stretch
monthly: offer a wide form across sites and counters
add: a per-day 'peak signature' tool giving each direction's AM/PM peak ratio over time, to match directions across counter replacements and catch label swaps
a per-channel view with a stable channel index, to spot one of the four piezo channels dying

summary: Liverpool St (N) E of Kent St was counted by Ecocounter 228 (2016-2024) and Metrocount 357 (from Oct 2025). The record has dead periods of exact zeros (Mar-Aug 2023, Dec 2024-Jun 2025), several shorter outages and intermittent sensor failures (Dec 2023, Mar 2024), and feed-level whole-day duplicates in 2022-2024; the near-zero weekends and the week in 2017-2019 carry a trickle of riders and look like real path closures, so they are kept. Counter 357's direction labels are reversed relative to 228's (its 'West' carries the morning peak), and the four counter-directions are kept as separate series because the level across the replacement cannot be checked.
